bank_access: Effectively blocked: banks require in-person KYC, local address and visa, and international correspondent banking has largely collapsed under sanctions; a remote foreign NGO founder has no realistic path.

No remote opening. Banks (BML, MIB) require an in-person branch visit with passport, valid work/residence visa and a local address; a foreign founder with no presence would need a local agent to apply.
CBN rules require a Bank Verification Number (BVN) - biometric enrolment only in Nigeria - plus CERPAC residence card and local address for foreigners; opening from abroad is not possible.

Bank of Ghana KYC requires a non-citizen Ghana Card (biometric ID) and a GhanaPostGPS local address; foreigners must open the account in person, so a remote founder needs a local visit or representative.

BCEAO/UEMOA AML rules apply; banks mainly open accounts in branch, and non-residents typically need a local address or in-person KYC - a remote foreign founder would need a local visit or representative.
No remote opening. Banks require in-person account opening with passport, proof of local address and residency/work permit; a foreign founder with no presence needs a local agent to act in person.
In-person opening is the norm: passport plus residence or work permit (non-ECOWAS foreigners face heavier scrutiny) and local address under BCEAO rules; remote opening is not available.
No remote opening. Foreigners must apply in person with passport, residence/work permit and proof of local address; a remote founder has no path and needs a local representative to open the account.
Banks require in-person KYC: passport, residence permit and proof of local address under BCEAO AML rules; no remote account opening, so a foreign founder needs a local visit or agent.
In-person opening required; non-residents and diaspora may open accounts with extra documentation, but physical presence and local papers are typical - a remote founder needs a local visit or agent.
Banking is paper-based and requires physical presence at a Bissau bank; passport plus residence permit, low digitalization. A remote foreign founder has no realistic remote path - local agent needed.
BCEAO rules: non-resident accounts need central-bank approval and banks demand in-person KYC (notarized ID, proof of funds) after 2024 AML tightening; remote opening is effectively unavailable.
No remote opening. CBG-supervised banks require an in-person visit with passport, visa/residence permit and proof of address; a remote foreign founder needs a local visit or representative.

Bank of Sierra Leone requires a NIN for new individual accounts, and foreign corporate account openings need a residence permit plus in-person KYC; remote opening is not available - local visit required.
No remote opening. Banks require in-person identity verification with passport, residence permit and proof of address; a foreign founder with no presence needs a local agent to open the account.
No remote opening. Banks require in-person application with passport, residence permit and proof of local address; a foreign founder with no presence needs a local visit or representative.
Effectively blocked: no independent civil-society sector exists - all social organizations are state/party organs, and foreign entities have no access to the state-controlled banking system.

Foreigners with legal stay can open accounts in person (Law 395-1), but a remote founder has no such grounds, and sanctions isolate Russian banks from SWIFT - access is effectively blocked for foreigners abroad.
